request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person row and the sheet rollup now show a settled-total and an open-total. `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in the spec.

**How they're worked out.** The calculation lives in the front end, so nothing changed on the server or in the stored data.
- **Person:** the totals use the same counted claims as the due-total, so held, deferred and retired-and-excluded claims are left out. The settled-total is the sum over their SETTLED claims, at the frozen figure each was settled at, corrections included. The open-total is the sum over their OPEN and PENDING claims, late charges included. Neither is capped, so the two add up to the person's due-total before the cap.
- **Sheet:** `rollup-settled-total` and `rollup-open-total` are simply everyone's figure added up. They are not trimmed and not capped.

**One behaviour you might not assume:** when a person has no rate and their due-total shows "n/a", both new totals show `0.00`, not "n/a". At first I showed "n/a" there, but the test expects `0.00`, the same way the person's excess already shows `0.00` in that case.

**Files changed:**
- `features/claims/claims.slot.tsx`: the person's two new cells and their column headers.
- `features/claims/useSheetTotals.ts`: the sheet's settled-total and open-total.
- `features/claims/rollup.slot.tsx`: shows the two sheet totals in the rollup.
